<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>We study the topology of toric maps. We show that if <jats:inline-formula id="j_crelle-2015-0104_ineq_9999_w2aab3b7b3b1b6b1aab1c16b1b1Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mrow>
                              <m:mi>f</m:mi>
                              <m:mo>:</m:mo>
                              <m:mrow>
                                 <m:mi>X</m:mi>
                                 <m:mo>→</m:mo>
                                 <m:mi>Y</m:mi>
                              </m:mrow>
                           </m:mrow>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="graphic/j_crelle-2015-0104_eq_0544.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>{f\colon X\to Y}</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula> is a proper toric morphism, with <jats:italic>X</jats:italic> simplicial, then
the cohomology of every fiber of <jats:italic>f</jats:italic> is pure and of Hodge–Tate type. When the map is a fibration, we give an explicit formula for the Betti numbers
of the fibers in terms of a relative version of the <jats:italic>f</jats:italic>-vector,
extending the usual formula for the Betti numbers of a simplicial complete toric variety. We then describe the Decomposition Theorem
for a toric fibration, giving in particular a nonnegative combinatorial invariant attached to each cone in the fan of <jats:italic>Y</jats:italic>, which is positive
precisely when the corresponding closed subset of <jats:italic>Y</jats:italic> appears as a support in the Decomposition Theorem. The description of this invariant involves
the stalks of the intersection cohomology complexes on <jats:italic>X</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Y</jats:italic>, but in the case when both <jats:italic>X</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Y</jats:italic> are simplicial, there is a simple formula
in terms of the relative <jats:italic>f</jats:italic>-vector.</jats:p>
title: Combinatorics and topology of proper toric maps
